_doc: Pieces Townsfolk.backstory() assembles into two or three sentences for every generated person: who they are (by archetype), their work or family, and one thing the rink knows about them. Tokens: {first} {surname} {town} {job} {employer} {kid} {kids} {partner} {grandkid} {parent} {friend} {years} {since} {fav} {age}. A line whose token has nothing to fill it is skipped. Tone: warm, a little satirical, never cruel (LORE.md, PATHS.md).

hockey_parent: {first} has driven {kid} to more 6 a.m. practices than the bus has routes.
{first} learned the offside rule in a week out of self-defence and now explains it to other parents, loudly.
{first} owns four travel mugs and a seat cushion with {kid}'s number on it.
{first} keeps a spare neck guard, a spare skate lace and a spare opinion in the glovebox.
figure_parent: {first} can tell a double toe from a double flip at forty metres and won't, out of politeness.
{first} has sewn more sequins onto {kid}'s dresses than anyone should have to.
{first} is on the six a.m. coffee bench, second thermos from the left.
{first} has read the test-day rules twice and the club newsletter once, under protest.
rink_rat: {first} is at the rink so much the vending machine knows {first}'s order.
{first} has never paid for public skate and has never once been asked to.
{first} knows which door sticks, which drain gurgles and where Earl hides the good shovel.
{first} wants to drive the resurfacer more than anything, including dessert.
beer_leaguer: {first} has played beer league in the valley for {years} years and peaked in about the second one.
{first} brings a cooler, a stick from 2009 and an unshakeable belief in the wrist shot.
{first} hasn't missed a Tuesday since the team got its own jerseys.
{first} plays defence because nobody else on the team would.
retiree_regular: {first} retired in {retired} and has been at the rink every week since, mostly for the coffee.
{first} remembers when the snack bar sold cigarettes and still thinks the fries were better then.
{first} has an opinion about every renovation since 1974, and a bench.
{first} sits in the same seat every week and considers it, legally, theirs.
date_night: {first} is here with {partner} because the movie theatre in {town} closed in 2011.
{first} met {partner} at a public skate, which {partner} remembers differently.
{first} pretends not to be able to skate so {partner} has to hold on.
{first} and {partner} are trying something new this year, and the something is ice.
figure_skater: {first} has landed the axel in practice nine times and in front of {parent} zero times.
{first} is working toward a test day that {parent} has circled on the fridge in red.
{first} practises spins in the kitchen in socks, which is how the lamp broke.
{first} is the youngest skater in the club who can do a layback, and knows it.
minor_player: {first} plays for the Millbrook Minor Mallards and is convinced the coach has a system.
{first} wants to play in the Grand Northern like Ronnie Haverstock, or failing that, drive a truck.
{first} has a lucky roll of tape that is now mostly lucky and very little tape.
{first} asks for the puck from every game, including the ones they lost.
teen: {first} is in grade {grade} at Millbrook High and would like that to be over, eventually.
{first} comes to the rink for the hot chocolate and to be seen not caring about anything.
{first} has a group chat with {friend} that is ninety percent rink gossip.
{first} is saving up for a car with roughly the money you'd need for a wheel.
learn_to_skate_adult: {first} decided at {age} that it was time to learn, and the ice has opinions about it.
{first} signed up for adult lessons after promising {kid} they'd skate together one day.
{first} grew up somewhere without winter and is still a little offended by this one.
{first} holds the boards like they owe {first} money, and is getting better every week.
stick_and_puck_regular: {first} shows up to every stick and puck with a bucket of pucks and no plan.
{first} has been working on the same toe drag since the spring.
{first} played junior B for half a season and talks about it for the other half of every year.
{first} comes for the empty ice and stays to complain that it's not empty.
broomballer: {first} plays broomball in running shoes and treats it like an Olympic event.
{first} joined the Harlow Falls Broomball Club for the social side and stayed for the bruises.
{first} has explained broomball to six people this year and converted two.
{first} owns more broom than broom handle, after the incident.
superfan: {first} has had Lumber Kings season tickets since {since} and a voice for about as long.
{first} brings a cowbell, a sign and an air horn the league has written to them about.
{first} has never once agreed with a referee and is proud of it.
{first} knows every player's mother's name and uses them.
autograph_hunter: {first} has a binder of signed cards and a pen in every coat pocket.
{first} once got Barry Pomeroy to sign a pizza box, and the box is framed.
{first} waits by the dressing room door with a Sharpie and an extraordinary amount of patience.
{first} can tell you which Dukes sign nicely and which ones sign like doctors.
coffee_coach: {first} coaches {kid}'s team from the stands, which the actual coach has mentioned.
{first} played midget AA in 1996 and it shows in every sentence.
{first} has a whiteboard in the car. Nobody knows why it's in the car.
{first} brings coffee for the coaches, which makes it harder for them to ask {first} to stop.
grandparent: {first} drives in from {town} to watch {grandkid} and brings butterscotch candies for the whole bench.
{first} knits a scarf in the team colours every season and hands them out to whoever looks cold.
{first} played on this ice in 1962 and says it was colder then, and better.
{first} is the only person in the stands who claps for the other team's goals, too.
scout: {first} scouts the valley for a junior club two provinces over and writes everything in a little notebook.
{first} drinks the rink coffee black and doesn't wince, which is how you know they're a professional.
{first} has watched more U15 hockey than anyone alive and says nothing about any of it.
{first} wears a team jacket from a club that folded in 2014, for luck.
shift_worker: {first} works shifts at {employer} and comes to the rink at hours nobody else does.
{first} sleeps in the afternoons, skates at noon and eats breakfast at nine at night.
{first} brings a lunch pail to the rink out of habit.
{first} knows exactly how long a flood takes, because {first} has watched about four hundred.
shopkeeper: {first} runs a shop on Main Street in {town} and closes it early for the playoffs.
{first} puts the Lumber Kings schedule in the shop window every September.
{first} sponsors a minor hockey team and checks the crest every game to make sure it's straight.
canteen_worker: {first} works the Hot Stove and can make change for a fifty in the dark.
{first} knows who wants extra gravy before they ask.
{first} has been told by Lorraine three times how to do the fries, and does them better.
volunteer: {first} sells 50/50 tickets with the persistence of a tax collector.
{first} runs the clock at minor hockey and has never once missed a buzzer.
{first} is on four committees, two of which meet at the rink.
{first} has volunteered so long nobody remembers asking.
official: {first} has reffed in the valley for {years} years and been called blind in every arena in it.
{first} has a whistle on a lanyard and a day job at {employer} that is quieter.
{first} carries a rule book in the bag and has never had to open it in an argument.
{first} refs because somebody has to, and because the money buys skate sharpening.
coach: {first} coaches because a coach once believed in {first}, and that coach was a lot like this.
{first} has a clipboard with every line combination since 2015 on it.
{first} works at {employer} and coaches nights, which means {first} is mostly coffee.
{first} gives the same speech before every game and the kids say it along with them.
rink_staff: {first} works the rink and can tell the ice temperature by the sound of a skate.
{first} has keys to doors that no longer exist.
{first} knows where every mop in the building is, and who took the good one.
any: {first} grew up in {town} and never quite left.
{first} moved to {town} for a job and stayed for reasons that are mostly the rink.

work: {first} works as {job_a} at {employer} and plans the week around the rink schedule.
Weekdays belong to {employer}; the rink gets the rest.
{first}'s hours at {employer} decide which games {first} makes and which ones {first} hears about on the radio.
retired: {first} retired from {employer} and immediately got busier.
Retired now, {first} has time for every event the rink puts on, and an opinion on each.

partner: {partner} is usually somewhere nearby, holding the coffee.
{first} and {partner} have been married long enough to argue about the same penalty for a decade.
kids: {kids} keep {first}'s calendar full and the car smelling like hockey bags.
grandkids: {grandkid} is the light of {first}'s life and the reason for the seat cushion.
kid: {parent} drives {first} to the rink and pretends to read in the car.
{parent} is the one in the stands wearing {first}'s old jersey.
single: {first} lives alone with a dog that has more hockey opinions than most people.
{first} says the rink is the most social thing in the week, and means it.

rink: {first} likes {fav} best and would never say so to the {fav2} crowd.
Ask {first} about the 2005 night the Cup came to Millbrook. Or don't, if you're in a hurry.
{first} has a favourite spot on the glass by the penalty box and will tell you why.
{first} claims to have seen Doris start on the first try once. Nobody believes it.
{first} always buys a coffee and never drinks the last third.
{first} still talks about the year the heaters worked.
{first} has strong feelings about the canteen fries, all of them positive.
{first} once found a puck from 1988 under the bleachers and keeps it in the car.
{first} is suspicious of composite sticks, on principle.
{first} reads every notice on the corkboard, including the ones from 2014.
{first} thinks the new owner seems all right. For now.
{first} keeps a mitten in each coat pocket and has never found a pair.
